page.description: openSUSE editions and architectures: the Leap 16.0 fixed release and the Tumbleweed rolling snapshot, with official images and a ROMinit USB walkthrough.
page.eyebrow: OPERATING SYSTEM / ENTERPRISE-BASED AND ROLLING LINUX
page.intro: Two openSUSE tracks on one page: Leap, the fixed release built from SUSE’s enterprise code base and supported for years, and Tumbleweed, the rolling snapshot tested release by release. Pick the track, then an image.
pros: Leap is a slow-moving release with long support; Tumbleweed rolls with tested snapshots.
YaST and zypper cover installation, updates and system configuration on both tracks.
Btrfs snapshots and rollback by default in recent releases.
Installers for x86_64, with aarch64 and i686 media on Tumbleweed.
cons: Newer software arrives later than on Tumbleweed, and Tumbleweed expects regular maintenance.
Tumbleweed has no long support window; Leap is the fixed-release sibling.
Leap media ships SHA-512 only and Tumbleweed’s screenshots are not 16.0, so coverage differs per track.
The offline images are several gigabytes; the network installer needs a working connection.
page.previewNote: A stock screenshot of openSUSE Leap 15.4 with GNOME from Wikimedia Commons. It is not 16.0 and not a ROMinit recording: no image was written to a USB stick and nothing was booted for this page.

shot.alt: openSUSE Leap 15.4 GNOME desktop with the activities overview
shot.caption: Stock screenshot of openSUSE Leap 15.4 · not 16.0, no USB written, no boot tested.

page.status: Write the Leap offline installer or a Tumbleweed image to a USB stick and boot it; the installer partitions the target disk. Writing erases the stick, and the install erases the chosen partitions. Leap media is published with SHA-512, so ROMinit offers the download but not USB preparation for it.

editions.name: Leap 16.0 offline installer
editions.description: The full installation image, carrying the packages needed to install without a network.
editions.usbNote: 4.5 GB image: use a stick that fits it. Write it with dd or any image writer; writing erases the stick.

editions.name: Offline DVD (x86_64)
editions.description: The full offline installer with the complete package set.
editions.usbNote: 4.7 GB image. Write it with dd or any image writer; writing erases the stick.

editions.name: Network installer (x86_64)
editions.description: A small installer that downloads packages during installation.
editions.usbNote: 418 MB image. Write it with dd or any image writer; writing erases the stick, and the install needs a network connection.
